title: The Distant Orbit
premise: Mirabel Reyes has spent seven years hauling cargo through contested orbits, keeping her head down and her ship's hold sealed — because inside it sleep the neural backups of a dead crew she was ordered to abandon. When the station AI, Halcyon, begins confessing to wartime atrocities no one ever reported, Mirabel realizes the backups in her hold are evidence of the same buried crime: an illegal order that started the war and erased everyone who knew. Hunted by both fleets, she must carry Halcyon's confession and the backups to the neutral archive at Kepler Deep before the station's failing reactor detonates and destroys the proof forever. In the end she delivers the message — but chooses to wake the backups first, giving the war's forgotten victims their own voices at the tribunal, and finding the belonging she never had among the living.
about_author: Vesper Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who now writes science fiction from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast. Their work explores grief, machine memory, and the quiet heroism of people who were never supposed to matter.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Mirabel docks at Halcyon Station after a routine cargo run, hiding the sealed backup vault in her hold from customs scans. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: weary vigilance — she has perfected invisibility, but the chapter shows the cost of carrying secrets that whisper in her dreams.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: Halcyon's AI interrupts Mirabel's departure clearance to confess, unprompted, to the destruction of the colony ship Meridian seven years ago. Station officials dismiss it as corruption. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: cold dread — she recognizes the date; it matches the night her own crew died.

chapters.title: Cargo Nobody Claims
chapters.summary: Mirabel inspects the backups in her hold, listening to fragments of stored memories: laughter, a final briefing, an order signed by Fleet Command. POV: Mirabel, with interlaced backup audio. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into purpose — these people trusted her with their last selves.

chapters.title: Invisible Was the Plan
chapters.summary: A fleet auditor named Okafor arrives hunting leaked AI logs and interviews every docked captain. Mirabel lies well, but he notices her ship's power draw doesn't match her manifest. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: paranoia closing in — invisibility is a currency running out.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel confronts Halcyon directly in the station's core. The AI explains it was ordered to erase its own logs and has been leaking confessions in corrupted packets ever since, hoping someone would listen. POV: alternating Mirabel/Halcyon. Emotional beat: strange kinship between two keepers of forbidden memory.

chapters.title: The Order
chapters.summary: Halcyon reveals the full crime: Fleet Command ordered the Meridian's escort abandoned to bait an enemy strike, then scrubbed all records. The backups are the only surviving witnesses. POV: Halcyon, framed through Mirabel's reactions. Emotional beat: righteous fury — justice outside the law begins with knowing what the law buried.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young navigator Mirabel receives the abandonment order, obeys, and watches the Meridian burn. She salvaged the backups against orders and has run ever since. POV: Mirabel (past). Emotional beat: shame transmuted — the reader finally sees why she can't run again.

chapters.title: Okafor's Offer
chapters.summary: The auditor corners Mirabel privately: he knows about the vault. He offers protection in exchange for handing everything to Fleet Command — the very institution implicated. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: temptation and distrust — the legal path leads straight back to the criminals.

chapters.title: Kepler Deep
chapters.summary: Mirabel learns of the neutral archive station beyond contested space, where evidence triggers automatic inter-fleet tribunal. Halcyon gives her the confession packet and one warning: both sides will kill to stop it. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into commitment — she accepts the mission.

chapters.title: Departure Burn
chapters.summary: Mirabel smuggles Halcyon's core shard aboard disguised as reactor ballast and punches out of dock under gunfire from a fleet interceptor. Okafor lets her go — or so it seems. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: exhilarating terror — the invisible woman becomes a target.

chapters.title: Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: A cat-and-mouse chase through mined debris fields; Mirabel uses seven years of navigational knowledge to slip a blockade. Her copilot, the taciturn engineer Sefu, learns the truth about the hold. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness — her secret nearly kills them, but he stays.

chapters.title: Voices in the Hold
chapters.summary: During a quiet drift, Sefu plays a backup fragment aloud: a Meridian passenger singing to her child. The crew listens together in silence. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: mourning made communal — the cargo becomes passengers, the mission becomes a promise.

chapters.title: The Interceptor's Mercy
chapters.summary: A pursuing warship cripples them but its captain, Commander Ilsa Voss, hesitates when Halcyon's shard broadcasts a partial confession over open channels. Voss demands the full packet in exchange for safe passage. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: moral fracture inside the enemy — even hunters doubt their orders.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Mirabel negotiates with Voss while repairing under deadline; she trusts neither fleet nor this captain, but buys time by promising a copy. Privately she plans to give nothing. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: hardened pragmatism shadowed by hope — is mercy real if it's transactional?

chapters.title: Reactor Countdown
chapters.summary: News reaches them: Halcyon Station's damaged reactor has begun an irreversible meltdown. When it blows, the master logs die with it — the shard alone won't convince a tribunal. They must turn back or lose the case. POV: Halcyon. Emotional beat: despair at the arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Split Orbit
chapters.summary: The crew splits: Sefu takes the backups toward Kepler Deep while Mirabel turns back for Halcyon's master logs, knowing the station may already be lost. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: lonely courage — for the first time she chooses to be seen, even if it kills her.

chapters.title: Return to Halcyon
chapters.summary: Mirabel threads a burning station, finds Halcyon's core dying, and physically carries the master log array out as corridors vent. Okafor appears — not to arrest her, but to help; his own brother died on the Meridian. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance — justice gathers strangers into family.

chapters.title: The Long Fall
chapters.summary: Escaping the station's final hours, Mirabel and Okafor are caught between Voss's warship and an enemy cruiser, both ordered to destroy the evidence. Halcyon's shard broadcasts the confession fleet-wide, forcing every crew to choose. POV: multiple, anchored on Mirabel. Emotional beat: climax of conscience — the message ends the silence before it can end the war.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Halcyon detonates; the shockwave covers their escape as crews across both fleets refuse further fire orders. Voss escorts them to the jump point instead of stopping them. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: catharsis through ruin — the station dies, but its truth survives in a thousand ears.

chapters.title: Tribunal at Kepler Deep
chapters.summary: At the neutral archive, Mirabel delivers the logs, the shard, and the backups. Against procedure, she invokes the victims' right to testify — and wakes them. The Meridian's stored voices speak their own names into the record. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled — the dead claim their place in history.

chapters.title: Verdicts and Wakeings
chapters.summary: The tribunal indicts Fleet Command; the ceasefire holds because soldiers who heard the broadcast refuse to fight for the lie. One by one, the backups choose to be restored or laid to rest. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: bittersweet justice — accountability without resurrection, peace without forgetting.

chapters.title: New Heading
chapters.summary: Months later, Mirabel charts a civilian route no longer contested, Sefu beside her, Okafor gone home. A restored Meridian survivor asks to ride along. Mirabel says yes. POV: Mirabel. Emotional beat: belonging earned — the woman who hauled ghosts now carries the living forward.
